psyPatient.definition: Personality: patient, plays the long game. YES when the ability's main payoff only comes after waiting: a once-per-game action the player times themselves (Slayer, Artist, Seamstress, Assassin, Judge...), a trigger on a later death or condition (Ravenkeeper, Sage, King, Scarlet Woman, Mastermind, Pixie), a fixed later night or day (Summoner, Xaan, Riot, Leviathan), or a choice to hold back (Po, Zombuul). NO when the ability pays out from the start or on every night or day with an immediate effect, leaving nothing to save up (start-knowing info, nightly info, nightly kills and poisons, day-1-only or night-1-only actions, always-on passives). Borderline: abilities that only trigger on your own death without a choice, borrowed or believed abilities, and characters whose waiting is incidental.

psyRiskTaker.definition: Personality: risk-taker. YES when the ability makes the player stake their own life, their exposure or their team's win on an uncertain call they choose to make (Gambler, Acrobat, Exorcist, Nightwatchman, Gossip, Ogre, Golem, Klutz, Puzzlemaster, Wizard, Goblin, Harlot). NO when using the ability is safe for the player, or the ability is passive with nothing the player chooses to stake (private info, protection, poison, passive outsider liabilities, vote modifiers). Borderline: public but downside-free actions (Slayer, Alsaahir, Juggler), forced death triggers (Moonchild), and evil abilities with only incidental exposure.

psyNeedsControl.definition: Personality: likes to be in charge. YES when the ability lets the player dictate rules or decisions for other players: who may act or use an ability (Preacher, Courtier, Witch), how votes count or who votes or nominates (Thief, Bureaucrat, Organ Grinder, Bishop, Voudon), who is executed (Judge, Vizier), where people sit (Matron), what others must claim (Cerenovus, Harpy), or which characters exist (Pit-Hag, Engineer, Summoner, Kazali). NO when the ability is passive, merely receives information, or puts the player at the mercy of others or the Storyteller (Butler, Zealot, Drunk, Atheist, info roles, passive Minions like Baron or Spy). Borderline: plain killers, protectors and borrowed abilities.

psyShowman.definition: Personality: loves the spotlight. YES when the ability is used in public or makes the player the visible centre of the action: public statements, guesses, kills or choices (Gossip, Juggler, Slayer, Alsaahir, Cult Leader, Klutz, Moonchild, Psychopath, Goblin, Gunslinger, Gangster), announcing deaths (Banshee), being publicly known (Vizier), spectacle (Boomdandy, Riot, Yaggababble), or performing (Pixie's madness, Deviant). NO when the ability is entirely private and works best if nobody notices the player (most Minions and night-killing Demons, Spy, Lunatic, Mutant, Damsel, Magician, Choirboy). Borderline: good info roles and protectors, which can go either way, and evil characters only known to be in play (Leviathan, Al-Hadikhia, Fearmonger).

psyDeceiver.definition: Personality: enjoys bluffing. YES when playing the character well means lying about who you are: every Minion and Demon that knows it is evil (except the publicly known Vizier and the Goblin, who claims openly), plus good characters that must pretend (Pixie's madness, Mutant, Damsel). NO for good characters whose ability rewards honesty, plus characters who believe they are something else (Marionette, Lunatic, Drunk). Travellers are borderline: their alignment is assigned and may be either.

psyManipulator.definition: Personality: pulls strings behind the scenes. YES when the ability secretly tampers with what other players know or can do without them choosing it: drunkenness, poison, madness, false information or hidden character and alignment changes (Poisoner, Pukka, No Dashii, Vigormortis, Widow, Xaan, Vortox, Lleech, Sailor, Innkeeper, Courtier, Philosopher, Magician, Mezepheles, Cerenovus, Harpy, Pit-Hag, Witch, Cacklejack). NO when the ability never affects anyone else's information or abilities (pure info roles, plain killers, protectors, passive self-only outsiders). Borderline: indirect or public effects (Minstrel, Preacher, Engineer, Goon, Sweetheart, Poppy Grower, Kazali, Snake Charmer).

psySelfless.definition: Personality: puts others first. YES when the ability's main value goes to other players, at no gain or at a cost to the player: protecting others (Monk, Innkeeper, Tea Lady, Pacifist, Devil's Advocate), exposing or sacrificing yourself for the team (Exorcist, Nightwatchman, Scapegoat, Goblin), reviving or empowering others (Professor, Bone Collector, Farmer, Summoner, Boffin, Gnome, Princess). NO when the ability is built around the player's own survival or personal victory (Soldier, Sailor, Fool, Mayor, Politician, Zombuul, Vizier, Deviant, Lleech, Psychopath, Scarlet Woman, Goon). Borderline: info roles, plain killers, and death triggers.

psyLoneWolf.definition: Personality: lone wolf. YES when the ability isolates the player: they don't know or may change their alignment (Ogre, Goon, Marionette), switch sides alone (Politician), play an inverted game (Heretic), or must hide what they are from everyone (Mutant, Damsel). NO when the ability is built on cooperation with specific allies (Cult Leader, Choirboy, Grandmother, Tea Lady, Butler, High Priestess, Steward, Knight, Summoner, Boffin, Kazali, Lil' Monsta, Vigormortis, Lord of Typhon, Legion). Borderline: everyone else.

psyCurious.definition: Personality: curious, needs to know. YES when the ability's main purpose is learning hidden information (every Townsfolk info role, Fisherman, Juggler, Ravenkeeper, Sage, Choirboy, Spy, Widow, Wraith, Harlot). NO when the ability never gives the player any information. Borderline: abilities where information is a side effect or depends on borrowing (Gambler, Acrobat, Exorcist, Amnesiac, Pixie, Godfather, Puzzlemaster, Beggar, Barista, Philosopher, Cannibal, Alchemist, Hermit, Apprentice).

psyIntuitive.definition: Personality: trusts the gut. YES when the ability asks the player to commit to a guess or judgement call that the ability gives them no evidence for (Gambler, Juggler, Amnesiac, Alsaahir, Puzzlemaster, Klutz, Moonchild, Golem, Slayer, Huntsman, Preacher, Snake Charmer, Exorcist, Courtier, Gossip, Ogre, Ojo). NO when the ability simply hands the player facts or works without any judgement (start-knowing and nightly info roles, passives, evil characters with full knowledge of their team). Borderline: killers choosing victims and other free choices.

psyPuzzler.definition: Personality: loves logic puzzles. Applies to information roles only. YES when the information arrives as a puzzle that needs deduction: one-of-several, counts, true-and-false mixes or partial clues (Chef, Empath, Investigator, Washerwoman, Librarian, Knight, Noble, Clockmaker, Shugenja, Balloonist, Chambermaid, Mathematician, Dreamer, Fortune Teller, Flowergirl, Town Crier, Oracle, Savant, Seamstress, Juggler, Sage, Amnesiac, Puzzlemaster). NO when the information is a direct answer (Steward, Grandmother, Bounty Hunter, Pixie, King, Undertaker, Artist, Fisherman, Ravenkeeper, Choirboy, Spy, Widow). Characters without information abilities are borderline.

psyProtective.definition: Personality: protective. YES when the ability keeps someone else alive or safe (Monk, Innkeeper, Tea Lady, Pacifist, Devil's Advocate, Exorcist, Princess, Professor, Huntsman, Scapegoat, Gnome). NO when the ability harms or kills others, or protects only the player themselves (killers, poisoners and madness-makers, Soldier, Sailor, Fool, Mayor, Zombuul). Borderline: info roles and passive outsiders.

psyChaosLover.definition: Personality: loves chaos. YES when the ability makes the game less predictable for everyone: it changes characters or alignments, causes random or mass deaths, inverts or breaks the rules, or scrambles votes and seats (Pit-Hag, Cacklejack, Barber, Hatter, Snake Charmer, Goon, Atheist, Heretic, Tinker, Plague Doctor, Gossip, Harpy, Mezepheles, Wizard, Xaan, Summoner, Boomdandy, Organ Grinder, Shabaloth, Kazali, Vortox, Legion, Al-Hadikhia, Riot, Thief, Matron, Voudon). NO when the ability brings order or certainty: reliable info, protection, steady passive effects, plain killing (info roles, Monk, Soldier, Mayor, Virgin, Fool, Tea Lady, Imp, No Dashii, Spy, Baron, Scarlet Woman). Borderline: everything in between.

psyLoyal.definition: Personality: loyal. YES when the ability ties the player to a particular other player or ally they stand by or serve (Butler, Grandmother, Choirboy, Tea Lady, Scarlet Woman, Mastermind, Boffin, Lil' Monsta's babysitters, Scapegoat, Gnome). NO when the player's allegiance shifts or the ability serves only themselves (Politician, Heretic, Goon, Ogre, Cult Leader, Snake Charmer, Soldier, Sailor, Fool, Zombuul, Lleech). Borderline: everyone else.

psyVengeful.definition: Personality: pays back wrongs. YES when the ability strikes back in response to something done to the player or their side: their death (Sage, Banshee, Moonchild, Choirboy for the King, Mastermind for the Demon), their nomination (Virgin), nominating or voting (Witch, Gunslinger, Gnome), an Outsider's death (Godfather) or their execution (Boomdandy). NO when the ability is purely defensive or forgiving (Monk, Innkeeper, Tea Lady, Soldier, Sailor, Fool, Pacifist, Devil's Advocate, Exorcist, Professor). Borderline: everyone else.

psyRuthless.definition: Personality: ruthless. YES when the character's own ability can directly kill a player: every Demon except the Leviathan, plus the Assassin, Godfather, Psychopath, Witch, Harpy, Boomdandy, Gossip, Slayer, Lycanthrope, Golem, Moonchild, Gunslinger, Gangster and Gnome. NO when the ability never causes anyone's death. Borderline: borrowed or believed abilities that might kill, extra executions (Butcher, Virgin, Judge, Vizier), and side-effect deaths (Pit-Hag, Harlot, Wizard).

psyPersuader.definition: Personality: persuader. YES when the ability only works if the player talks others into something: agreeing, saying a word, voting or executing their way, joining them, or believing their claim (Cult Leader, Mezepheles, Goblin, Mutant, Pixie, Evil Twin, Princess, Fearmonger, Vizier, Mastermind, Boomdandy, Harlot, Gangster, Beggar). NO when the ability works silently whatever anyone believes (night info, night kills, poison, protection, passives). Borderline: Gossip, Saint, Politician, Leviathan, Yaggababble, Deviant, Riot and others whose success leans on the table's mood.

psyUnderdog.definition: Personality: happy to be underestimated. YES when the ability looks harmless or stays invisible, then matters at a key moment, often after the player is overlooked or killed (Soldier, Fool, Virgin, Mayor, Magician, Poppy Grower, Farmer, Minstrel, Ravenkeeper, Sage, Choirboy, Banshee, Golem, Scarlet Woman, Mastermind, Zombuul). NO when the ability is loud, public or powerful from the outset (Slayer, Juggler, Gossip, Alsaahir, Cult Leader, Psychopath, Fearmonger, Vizier, Yaggababble, Al-Hadikhia, Riot, Leviathan, and the public Travellers). Borderline: everyone else.

psyImproviser.definition: Personality: improviser. YES when the ability is open-ended: the player decides what form it takes (choosing an ability, character, wish, question or statement) or must work out and adapt to what it is (Philosopher, Engineer, Artist, Gossip, Cannibal, Amnesiac, Hermit, Wizard, Pit-Hag, Summoner, Kazali, Bone Collector, Apprentice). NO when the ability has a single fixed function that works the same way every time. Borderline: abilities picked by the Storyteller, or partly flexible (Alchemist, Pixie, Courtier, Ojo, Cerenovus, Boffin, Barista).

psyContrarian.definition: Personality: contrarian. YES when the ability turns a normal expectation upside down (Heretic inverts the win, Thief makes votes count negatively, Devil's Advocate saves the condemned, Magician reads as the other team, Lycanthrope is a good killer, Atheist has no evil, Vortox makes truth false). NO when the ability makes the player go along with others (Zealot, Butler, Cult Leader, Goon, Ogre). Borderline: everyone else.
